\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb,amsthm}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\newtheorem{definition}{Definition}
\newcommand{\lean}[1]{}

\title{A Statement With Some Shape}
\author{A synthetic example}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:layout}\lean{Shape.layout}
Let $E$ be a nonempty type and $1 \le j \le k$. For every $x$ there is a constant $C$ such that,
for every $n$, both $x \le C$ and $n + x \le n + C$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:witnesses}\lean{Shape.witnesses}
For every $j$ there is a function $x$ with $x(j) = j$ and $j \le x(j)$, and there is a boolean
$x$ that is true.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:shapes}\lean{Shape.shapes}
Let $E$ be nonempty. No natural number is negative, and either every $n$ satisfies $0 \le n$ or,
if $1 = 1$, some $m$ equals $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}\label{def:multiple}\lean{Shape.MultipleAbove}\lean{Shape.fib}
A number $n$ is a multiple of $m$ above $b$ if $n = mq$ for some $q \ge b$. The Fibonacci numbers
are $F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$ and $F_{n+2} = F_n + F_{n+1}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:supplied}\lean{Shape.supplied}
Let $s$ be a solution for $d$ with bound at most $5$. Then $s$ starts at most at $5$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:assumed}\lean{Shape.assumed}
If every admissible datum has a good solution, then $0$ has a good solution.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:produced}\lean{Shape.produced}
Every admissible datum $d$ has a good solution.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:positive}\lean{Shape.positive}
Every positive number is at least $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:single}\lean{Shape.single}
A type with a single element has at most one element, and exactly one.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:probability}\lean{Shape.probability}
On a probability space, the whole space has measure one.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:none-large}\lean{Shape.none_large}
No solution for $0$ has a negative bound.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:two-solutions}\lean{Shape.two_solutions}
Two solutions $s$ and $t$ for the same datum start at the same point.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:both}\lean{Shape.both}
If $a \le b$ and $b \le a$, then $a = b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:jet}\lean{Shape.jet_lower}
If the first $n + 5$ differences of $f$ are bounded by $C$ on $S$, so are the first $n + 4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:below}\lean{Shape.below_succ}\lean{Shape.every_below}
A vector bounded by $i$ is bounded by $i + 1$; vectors bounded by $7$ are bounded by $8$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:steps}\lean{Shape.steps_pos}\lean{Shape.pick_at}
The number of steps down from $k + 3$ is positive, and $\mathrm{pick}(k + 1, 0) = 1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:conditional}\lean{Shape.conditional}
If every $x$ with $A(x)$ has some $y$ with $B(x, y)$, and $A(a)$ holds, then some $y$ has
$B(a, y)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:alternating}\lean{Shape.alternating}
For every $x$ there is $y$ such that $x + z \le y + z$ for every $z$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:premised}\lean{Shape.premised}
If $P$ holds, some $x$ is $0$; $Q$ holds exactly when some $n$ equals itself; and either some $x$
is $1$ or $Q$ holds.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:one-map}\lean{Shape.one_map}
Some map $\Phi \colon G \to H$ over $\mathbb{N}$ has both $A$ and $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}\label{def:digit}\lean{Shape.Digit.val}
The value of the digit $d_i$ is $i$, for $i = 0, \dots, 69$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:digit}\lean{Shape.last_digit}
The value of the digit $d_{69}$ is $69$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:digit-index}\lean{Shape.last_index}
A digit whose constructor index is $69$ has the value $69$.
\end{theorem}

\end{document}
